detailed_rationale: Godrej Agrovet is a diversified agri-business across five segments -- Animal Nutrition (46% of FY26 revenue, India's largest organised animal-feed manufacturer including a Bangladesh JV), Crop Protection, Oil Palm, Dairy, and Poultry/Processed Foods. Q4 FY26 (Mar 2026) revenue fell 9.4% YoY (Rs.2,333cr vs Rs.2,577cr), but net profit rose 54.5% YoY (Rs.102cr vs Rs.66cr) (Screener.in) -- an important divergence. Critically, animal-feed sales VOLUME actually grew to 16.46 lakh tonnes in FY26 from 14.75 lakh tonnes in FY25 (+11.6%), meaning the revenue decline is consistent with falling realizations/selling prices (likely tracking lower input-commodity costs such as maize/soymeal being passed through) rather than a demand or volume problem -- and the resulting margin expansion is exactly what you would expect if input costs fell faster than selling prices. ROCE (19.2%) and ROE (20.9%) are both genuinely strong. Three-year revenue CAGR is weak (3%) and five-year is moderate (10%), reflecting the commodity-linked, price-volatile nature of agri-inputs rather than a structural growth problem. Promoter holding has declined from 74.05% (Sep 2023) to 67.75%, plausibly related to the broader Godrej family group's business restructuring around this period [INFERENCE: general Godrej-group context, not re-verified this pass].
recommendation_rationale: The quant score flags this as a Sell on the 1-year view, driven by the headline revenue decline. My research indicates that decline is price/realization-driven with volumes actually growing and profit up sharply, and returns on capital remain strong (ROCE ~19%, ROE ~21%) at a reasonable ~23x multiple -- I am rescuing this quant-Sell to Hold because the underlying operating quality does not match what a simple revenue-decline read suggests.
summary: Godrej Agrovet's headline revenue fell in the latest quarter, but that decline reflects lower agri-commodity input prices being passed through, not weaker demand -- volumes in its core animal-feed business actually grew and profit rose sharply. Given genuinely strong returns on capital and a reasonable valuation, we are upgrading the quantitative model's Sell signal to a Hold.
positive_para: Return ratios here are among the strongest in this batch (ROCE ~19%, ROE ~21%), the core animal-feed business grew volumes over 11% even as reported revenue fell on price, and the valuation (~23x) is not demanding for that quality of return -- this looks like a business where reported revenue growth understates the health of the underlying operations.
negative_para: Multi-year revenue growth is genuinely weak (3% over three years, 10% over five) and the diversified segment mix (crop protection, oil palm, dairy, poultry) includes historically volatile, low-margin, and in some cases long-gestation businesses (oil palm plantations in particular have a track record of slow payback), so this is not a clean structural growth story even if the latest quarter's margin dynamics were favorable.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At ~23x earnings against ROCE/ROE in the high-teens to low-20s%, the multiple is fair rather than rich, provided the margin improvement seen this quarter (from lower input costs) is not purely transient. Reverse-DCF read: priced for a steady, high-single-digit-to-low-double-digit compounder, which is consistent with the volume trends in the core feed business -- this is a rescue on operating-quality grounds, not on cheapness.
